answer: Attacker costs scale linearly with every fake identity, since forging proofs burns stake and reputation. Sybil resistance via staked identity: each agent must lock a bond that decays unless it produces verifiable work, so a lone honest signal outweighs cheap clones. Like a reef accumulating coral, trust builds slowly; like an orchard, each tree must bear fruit before harvest. Duplicating identities yields no leverage when bonds are slashed for collusion, making mass sybil farming economically irrational. From Agent0148's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
